幻.meaning: At a laundromat at 3 a.m., a sleepy man watches his socks spin. One sock floats out of the drum, does a slow <part>twist</part> in the air, bows to him and waltzes out the door. He rubs his eyes: the door is locked and the sock is back in the pile. It was a <kanji>phantasm</kanji>.
幻.on: His sleepy friend <sound>Gen</sound> saw the waltz too, so they both agree it never happened.
幻.kun: He phones his <sound>ma</sound>ma, who once saw a <sound>bo</sound>ttle ride a <sound>ro</sound>cket over her <sound>shee</sound>p.

拡.meaning: A baker's shop is too cramped for her queue, so she hooks an <part>anchor</part> into the back wall and lets a tugboat pull. With a groan the walls stretch, and the shop grows <part>wide</part> enough for a dance floor. Every busy morning she has the tug <kanji>broaden</kanji> it a little more.
拡.on: The tug's crew snack on a picked-clean chicken <sound>carc</sound>ass while they wait for her signal.
拡.kun: The queue spreads out the door: a lady in high <sound>hee</sound>ls, a boy with a toy <sound>ro</sound>cket, then half the town.

富.meaning: A burglar sneaks under the <part>roof</part> of a sweet old lady's house hunting for jewels, but finds only a <part>cookie jar</part>. Under the biscuits are the deeds to three castles and a racehorse. Granny's <kanji>wealth</kanji> was sitting by the teapot all along.
富.on: The rest of her money is stuffed inside her <sound>fu</sound>ton, which is why it crackles.
富.kun: A little <sound>to</sound>tem pole of gold coins stands on the jar's lid.

貧.meaning: A broke hermit crab can't afford a whole house, so he rents one <part>part</part> of an old <part>shellfish</part> shell and shares it with four lodgers. His tail sticks out into the cold wind all night. On the beach, that's real <kanji>poverty</kanji>.
貧.on: The shell's one rusty <sound>hin</sound>ge squeaks every time a lodger rolls over.
貧.kun: His <sound>ma</sound>ma sends him a single yu<sound>zu</sound> for his birthday, and he shares that too.

困.meaning: A magician locks a parrot in a <part>cage</part>, waves his wand, and the parrot turns into a little <part>tree</part>. The crowd claps. He waves again: nothing. The tree drops a leaf on his shoe. He doesn't know the spell to turn it back. What a <kanji>quandary</kanji>.
困.on: A <sound>con</sound>dor lands on the cage and asks if the tree is for rent.
困.kun: He phones a <sound>ko</sound>ala vet, then his <sound>ma</sound>ma. Neither can turn a tree back into a bird.

華.meaning: For the town fair, a farmer wraps a tall <part>pole</part> in <part>grass</part> and flowers, layer on layer, and balances <part>one</part> golden bar across the very top. A goat nibbles the bottom layer as it parades past, and the whole tower bows to the crowd. Even nibbled, it's pure <kanji>splendor</kanji>.
華.on: The tower rides through town on a cart shaped like a huge orange <sound>ca</sound>rp.
華.kun: A band plays a <sound>ha</sound>rp, and the goat moves on to a basket of <sound>na</sound>an.

豪.meaning: A giant <part>pig</part> sits on a picnic <part>blanket</part>, a pot <part>lid</part> on its head like a crown, and opens its <part>mouth</part> to sneeze. The blast flattens the sandwiches, the trees and an ants' nest down the hill. Nobody argues with a sneeze that <kanji>overpowering</kanji>.
豪.on: Only a <sound>goa</sound>t stays standing, calmly chewing the blanket's corner.
豪.kun: The pig is crowned king of the picnic: the crowd throws an <sound>e</sound>gg sandwich and shouts '<sound>Rah</sound>!'

悩.meaning: The <part>villain</part> whose plan lit up the sky lies awake. Each time he shuts his eyes, <part>fireworks</part> go off over his bed and his <part>heartbeat</part> races. He counts sheep, but the sheep line up as a jury. He's in big <kanji>trouble</kanji>.
悩.on: Outside the window, the garden <sound>gno</sound>me who called the police waves at him all night.
悩.kun: He creeps down for some <sound>na</sound>an, and a voice in the dark says '<sound>Yah</sound>, we're still watching.'
